title: First 10-Day skill ossification & mentor handoff playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a short experiment-run playbook to reduce early-stage skill ossification (new hires locking into narrow task patterns) and make the 0-10 day mentor handoff intentionally signal-driven. We think a brief, structured mentor pairing + active micro-experiments in the first 10 days will: reduce fixated workflows, accelerate cross-skill exposure, and increase signal for hiring managers when making early-scope adjustments.

Audience:
People Ops, Hiring Managers, Hiring Interview Panels, Engineering Mentors, New Hires.

Hypothesis (one-liner):
If we pair new hires with a rotating mentor sequence and run 3 targeted micro-tasks that require different skill dimensions within days 1–10, then hires will demonstrate broader capability signals and ramp faster on cross-cutting responsibilities.

Success metrics (what we will measure):
- Manager confidence score at day 10 (survey): target +0.5 vs baseline.
- % of hires who touch >=3 distinct code/practice areas in first 10 days: target 80%.
- Early task rework rate (first 30 days) down by 15%.
- New-hire NPS on onboarding experience at day 14: +10 pts.

Quick experiment design (3x micro-tasks):
- Micro-task A (Day 1–2): Repo read + 60-min pairing to run a small end-to-end smoke test and file the first minimal bug note. Goal: systems orientation + code navigation.
- Micro-task B (Day 3–5): Small infra/config or CI tweak that requires reading docs and submitting a single-line fix/PR. Goal: ops awareness.
- Micro-task C (Day 6–9): Short product/UX writeup: take a 1–2 screen flow, write a short improvement suggestion and acceptance criteria (1 page). Goal: cross-team communication.
Each micro-task has a one-hour mentor pairing window and a 30-min manager sync the following day.

Mentor rotation pattern (recommended):
- Day 0 (pre-start): Onboarding admin mentor (HR buddy) confirms accesses
- Day 1–2: Codebase mentor (engineer, different subteam than hire)
- Day 3–5: Infra/Platform mentor (SRE or infra engineer)
- Day 6–9: Product/PM or UX mentor (product adjacent)
- Day 10: Hiring manager + mentor wrap: run the day-10 signal review and adjust scope.
Notes: second mentor should be outside the hire's immediate pod when possible to maximize exposure.

Day-10 signal review (template):
- Inputs: micro-task artifacts (PRs, notes), mentor short feedback (bullet list), new-hire self-rating (3 bullets), pairing attendance logs.
- Outputs: manager decision: keep scope / broaden scope / narrow scope / escalate training.
- Required fields for the review: 1) three observed strengths, 2) one risk (skill gap), 3) two next actions (learning or role changes).

Interview/Rubric adjustments (for hires we intend to run through this flow):
- Add a scored axis for cross-domain curiosity (0–5) based on candidate examples. Weight 10% on final hire decision for roles that will participate in this experiment.
- Add an asynchronous take-home microtask (90 mins) focused on cross-cutting communication: doc + small code snippet. Use this as a pre-hire predictor for completing Micro-task C early.
- Interview note template: specifically ask for "a time you intentionally worked outside your core skill and what tradeoffs you managed". Capture as a short example in the candidate record.

Manager playbook (day-by-day summary):
- Pre-start: confirm mentor rotation and calendar invites; grant early shadow access.
- Day 1: ensure pairing scheduled; set first micro-task.
- Day 3: quick check — did micro-task B expose infra mismatch? If yes, route to infra mentor for remediation.
- Day 6: confirm product mentor engagement; reinforce cross-domain framing.
- Day 10: run signal review; pick next 30/60/90 tasks with explicit learning objectives.

Mentor quick template (30–45 minute pairing):
- 5 min: context and goals for session
- 20–30 min: watch the hire do the micro-work (pairing, screen-share), ask clarifying Qs
- 5–10 min: quick feedback + 1 suggested follow-up learning artifact (doc, PR, toy exercise)
- Deliverable: a 3-bullet mentor note saved to the shared folder.

Checklist for People Ops (implementation steps):
1) Add experiment to new hire packet and template the schedule.
2) Create a shared Google folder for artifacts (PR links, mentor notes).
3) Build a one-click calendar invite set for rotating mentors.
4) Update interview scorecards to include cross-domain curiosity axis.
5) Ship a day-10 signal review form (Google Form) and attach to hire folder.
6) Pilot with 6 hires across eng/product this quarter.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Mentor bandwidth — mitigated by short 30–45m windows and a roster of backup mentors.
- Risk: Too much cognitive load on new hire — mitigate by keeping micro-tasks scoped <= 5% of weekly capacity and framing as learning.
- Risk: Measurement noise — mitigate by requiring artifacts for each micro-task (PR, doc, or checklist).

Sample artifacts (what to save to the hire folder):
- PR link or repo path for micro-task A/B
- short doc (500–800 words) for micro-task C
- mentor three-bullet note file (plain text)
- day-10 signal review form response

Pilot checklist (week-of-launch):
- People Ops: email pilot cohort + managers, set up shared folders (done 1 week prestart)
- Recruiting: flag candidates who will be eligible for the experiment (flag in candidate note)
- Engineering leads: provide mentor roster and confirm availability
- Data: confirm a short survey for day-10 manager confidence and day-14 new-hire NPS

Open questions (to resolve during pilot):
- How to compensate mentors for time? (opt-in mentor hours credit or rotation duty?)
- Do we gate the experiment on role seniority? (prefer junior-mid vs senior)
- Should micro-tasks be role-specific templates or fully generic?

Next steps (immediate):
- Iterate this doc with Jordan/Kim and Priya to produce a 1-page manager cheat sheet (target Nov 10).
- Create Google Form for day-10 signal capturing fields (owner: Leila).
- Schedule pilot kick-off sync (30m) with recruiting + 3 hiring managers (owner: Priya).

Notes to self / rough edges (working doc):
- Keep micro-tasks intentionally tiny — we want signal, not production work.
- Emphasize artifact retention — artifacts are what make day-10 review actionable.
- Consider a small mentor recognition token (swag or kudos) for early adopters.

References and inspiration:
- Internal: onboarding-accelerator-playbook (Confluence), private-deployments-preboard-security-hardware-checklist.json (drive)
- External: "Deliberate Practice for Engineers" blog post (link in Confluence)

If this experiment looks good, I want to pilot with 4 new grads + 2 lateral hires in December.

-- Leila
